Three traps that win games under 1000, and the one move that stops each of them. Save it before your next game. ♟️

Which one caught you first? 👇

slides.title: Three traps
slides.sub: AND HOW NOT TO FALL FOR THEM
slides.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nc6 Qh5 Nf6 Qxf7#

slides.title: Scholar’s Mate
slides.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nc6 Qh5 Nf6 Qxf7#
slides.take: Queen and bishop both aim at f7, the one square only Black’s king defends. Nf6 attacks the queen but leaves f7 to fall.
slides.edge: The fix: 3…g6 blocks the attack and hits the queen. It has to move again while you keep developing.

slides.title: Légal Trap
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 Bc4 Bg4 Nc3 g6 Nxe5 Bxd1 Bxf7+ Ke7 Nd5#
slides.take: White gives up the queen on purpose. Taking it lets three minor pieces mate the king in the middle of the board.
slides.edge: The fix: when a free queen appears, check what happens after you take it. Here 5…dxe5 loses only a pawn.

slides.title: Blackburne Shilling
slides.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5 Nxf7 Qxg2 Rf1 Qxe4+ Be2 Nf3#
slides.take: Black leaves e5 hanging on purpose. Grabbing the pawn and then the rook walks White straight into a smothered mate on f3.
slides.edge: The fix: answer 3…Nd4 with 4.Nxd4 or simply castle. The pawn on e5 is bait.
